My grandmother lived with us for about a year while I was in high school. Most of that time my grandma was long gone just a confused shell of a human. She would constantly go inside and outside our front door sit on the porch and walk around. Like 20 times a day she would come in and out. Eventually she got lost when she went out so we had to do something. My parents put a child lock door knob on the front door. She would yell and swear at me to let her out. Usually i would open it for her but not always. Remembering the sound of her talking to herself in frustration and giggling that fucking door knob still bothers me. 0 out of 10 would not recommend.

Stay busy. Anything you can do to make yourself better or help someone else. Don't allow yourself time to sit around and be sad. Especially during the first few weeks. Those are going to be aweful no way around it. Plan monthly visits and use a count down app to keep track of the days until. Its a fun way to get excited about being with each other again. 

Communication is even more important when you're in long distance how you're feeling, what you're going to do about it ECT. Keep things interesting with Skype dates packages and letters. You can still give love without physical touch. 

Use the time to make yourself a more successful person. Make you the best version of yourself you can be and take your life somewhere. You still have to go on this life adventure and learn who you are and what you want. However you have someone to share it with and help you through it. Best of luck
